Reading this viewer

Each node is a region of interest from a 5-node dynamic causal model (DCM), fit per subject and taken to a group level with Parametric Empirical Bayes (PEB). The matrix shown is a Bayesian Model Average (BMA) over the search of nested models — A is intrinsic (task-independent) effective connectivity, B is the modulatory (task/condition-dependent) change in that connectivity.

An edge runs from the source region to the region it influences. Colour encodes the sign of the group-level effect (red = excitatory, blue = inhibitory); line weight and opacity scale with effect size and posterior probability. Diagonal (self) terms work differently: DCM fixes every region's self-connection as inhibitory and estimates only a log-scaling parameter on it (self-connection = −exp(Ep) Hz), so a positive Ep means stronger self-inhibition and a negative Ep means weaker self-inhibition (a more disinhibited, excitable region) — the opposite sense from an off-diagonal Ep. To keep red/blue meaning the same thing everywhere (red = toward excitation/disinhibition, blue = toward inhibition), self-connection rings are coloured by the opposite of their raw sign: a positive (more-inhibited) self-term draws blue, a negative (disinhibited) self-term draws red. Self terms are drawn as a ring around the node, not a line. The Amygdala is estimated as a single bilateral parameter — it is plotted at both its left and right MNI coordinates, each carrying the identical connectivity value.

Ep
Expected value of the parameter (BMA posterior mean), in Hz for A, unitless scaling for B. For diagonal (self) terms this is a log-scaling parameter on a fixed inhibitory self-connection, not a rate — positive = more inhibited, negative = disinhibited (see above).
SD
Posterior standard deviation of Ep — √diag(Cp), the BMA posterior covariance SPM returns alongside Ep, i.e. each parameter's own marginal uncertainty (ignores covariance between parameters).
Pp
Posterior probability the parameter is non-zero. Two methods are available, matching the SPM PEB review GUI — BMA search: evidence for models with the connection switched on vs off, compared across the reduced-model search (accounts for covariance among parameters, used by default). Marginal P>0: each parameter treated in isolation, from the area of its own Gaussian posterior (Ep, SD) above zero — ignores covariance, and can disagree with BMA search near threshold.
Covariates
Commonalities = group mean; Dep / Anx / Stress = mean-centred symptom severity; Age, Gender = nuisance covariates — all columns of the same PEB design matrix.
Load a different connectivity matrix

Bring your own network: a JSON file with nodes (name + MNI x/y/z) and a square matrix of connection strengths, optionally a matching pvalues matrix used as the evidence measure. Or a plain CSV of an N×N matrix — nodes are then placed in a generic ring layout and labelled Node 1…N.

{"nodes":[{"name":"Amygdala","x":-26,"y":2,"z":-20}, …], "matrix":[[0,0.42,…],…], "pvalues":[[1,0.98,…],…]}

Cortical surface: FreeSurfer fsaverage5 pial mesh (MNI-aligned) · region coordinates and labels as supplied for the CNBT depression & anxiety model · PEB search, BMA model 1
